references.text: Balaam repeats the same principle - he can only speak what the Lord puts in his mouth. This shows his understanding of prophetic speech.
Balaam confirms again that he must speak what the Lord says, regardless of what Balak wants.
Balaam explains that he cannot go beyond the Lord's word, neither for good nor for evil.
Moses' prophecy about a coming prophet whom God will put His words in the mouth of, parallel to Balaam's statement that God puts words in his mouth.
Jeremiah receives God's words placed in his mouth, using the same language as Balaam uses regarding prophetic inspiration.
Ezekiel is told to speak God's words to the people, in the same way that Balaam can only speak what God gives him.
Jesus promises that the Holy Spirit will give the disciples words to speak, parallel to how God put words in Balaam's mouth.
